newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian end lower, outlook uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Belgian end lower, outlook uncertain.

text.p: Belgian shares ended Tuesday's session easier, coming under pressure with neighbouring bourses from a reversal on Wall Street of the previous session's gains, and with neither bonds nor the dollar giving much direction.

"All European markets have been treading water all day," one dealer said. The prospect of a regular Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday and U.S. December jobs data on Friday were both serving to keep the markets cautious, but volumes were still up on last week with 2.8 billion francs of shares traded.
The Bel-20 index .BFX ended 6.82 points or 0.36 percent down at 1,891.94, the day's low, after peaking at 1,901.80.

Among the most heavily traded shares was retailer Delhaize, unchanged at 1,935 francs on a volume of 98,529 shares, with interest in the stock boosted by the prospect of provisional 1996 sales figures due to be released on Friday.
Analysts are confident of good news after U.S. unit Food Lion - which makes up two thirds or so of Delhaize's consolidated turnover - already announced strong fourth quarter sales.
Generale Bank analyst Sandra Vandersmissen said the share price would only be impacted by Friday's results if figures for sales in Belgium grew a greater-than-expected six percent or so.
Steel maker Cockerill Sambre, which received a visit from analysts on Tuesday, rose 4.7 percent or six francs to 133 wit 760,215 shares traded.

Dealers came up with no specific reasons for the rise but noted that cyclicals were among stocks seen performing well in 1997. Cockerill has been staging a slight rebound since December 20 but remains in an overall downtrend begun in September 1993 when the stock stood at 214 francs.
